beats.text: Before Parasite, Bong Joon Ho was a rich family's tutor.
His girlfriend taught their son English, and vouched for him as the math tutor. He says he was bad at math.
That's how the con in Parasite begins: a friend vouches for you.
He says it felt like peeping into strangers' lives.
That glass mansion? Not a real house. A set, built from scratch.
Parasite won the Palme d'Or, a first for Korea. At the Golden Globes, he urged us to overcome the one-inch tall barrier of subtitles.
Then four Oscars, including Best Picture, the first ever not in English.
The film's flood? Shot in a giant water tank.
Three years later, a real flood trapped a family in a Seoul semi-basement. Three died.
Seoul vowed to phase these homes out. About two hundred thousand households still live half underground.
